title: Jeju Air 2216: The Mound at the End of the Runway

scenes.text: Three minutes past nine in the morning, the twenty ninth of December, two thousand and twenty four. A Boeing seven three seven is sliding down a runway in the south west of South Korea on its belly, with no wheels down, in the wrong direction.
It is running out of runway. Two hundred and fifty metres past the end of it there is a low grassy mound with an aerial on top.

scenes.text: Frangible.
There is a word in airport design that decides this entire accident, and most people watching will never have needed to know it.
Frangible. Here is how the American regulator defines it, and the international standard says the same thing in different words.

Retains its structural integrity and stiffness up to a designated maximum load, but on impact from a greater load, breaks, distorts, or yields in such a manner as to present the minimum hazard to aircraft.
Read it again, because it is doing something very specific. It is not asking for a strong structure. It is requiring that past a certain load, the thing must give way.
The rule exists for exactly one reason. Aeroplanes sometimes leave the end of runways, and the things sitting near a runway have to break rather than stop them.

scenes.text: And there is a second thing in that same document, which I did not know before I read it, and which I think is the quietest and worst fact in this entire story.
The ground past the end of a runway is not spare ground. It has a name, and it has a defined purpose.
scenes.query: ILS localizer antenna array beside airport runway

scenes.text: It is called the runway safety area.
A defined surface surrounding the runway, prepared or suitable for reducing the risk of damage to aircraft in the event of an undershoot, overshoot, or excursion from the runway.
Read what that ground is for. It exists specifically for the case where an aeroplane leaves the runway. That is not an unforeseen event. It is the event the surface is designed around.
It is the one piece of an airport whose entire job is to be survivable.
